faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.

faqs.question: Can I use digital voicemail with my fax?
faqs.answer:
If your digital voicemail is provided by your phone company and is not a separate answering machine, you cannot use the product to automatically receive and print faxes. To receive faxes manually, turn off Auto Answer mode. Epson recommends that you use a separate answering machine connected to the
EXT
port on the product for best results.

faqs.question: Do I need a filter if I'm faxing over a DSL?
faqs.answer: Yes, you must connect the appropriate DSL filter or ISDN terminal adapter or router to the wall jack to use the line for faxing or voice calls on your product. Contact your DSL or ISDN provider for the necessary equipment.

faqs.question: How do I set up speed dialing for a single phone number or a group of phone numbers?
faqs.answer:
If you want to add single phone numbers to your speed dial list, you can do so
through the Setup menu on the CX11NF's control panel
or
through the Speed Dial Utility
(Windows only).
If you want to create a speed dial group for multiple phone numbers, you must
use the Speed Dial Utility
(Windows only).

faqs.question: Do I need to use a filter if I fax over a VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) line?
faqs.answer:
No, the filters are only required if you have DSL service.
Because fax machines are designed to work over standard analog telephone lines, Epson does not guarantee that fax transmission will work over VoIP phone lines (cable systems such as Cox, Charter, Time Warner, Comcast, FiOS, magicJack, and Vonage).
Internet traffic can interfere with faxing because VoIP communicates through the internet and not through standard analog telephone lines. The data sent over the internet for a fax is digitized into packets and this process can cause data loss.
You can try slowing the transmission speed of the fax by setting ECM on the product to
Off
and selecting a slower Fax Speed. If this does not help, contact your VoIP service provider for help.
For more information, please contact your telephone service provider.

faqs.question: How often should I clean my product?
faqs.answer:
The product needs only minimal cleaning. When print quality has decreased, scan quality has decreased, or there is trouble with paper feeding, cleaning the CX11NF may solve the problem. See
Cleaning the Product

Follow these steps to verify whether a TCP/IP address has been obtained:
Press the
Setup
button.
At the
Printer Settings
option, press the
button.
At the
Information
option, press the
button.
Use the
button to select
Network Status Sheet
, then press the
button. The CX11NF will print a status sheet.
On the status sheet, check the second item in the
TCP/IP
section and verify that the IP address has a number such as the example shown below:
IP Address
135.792.46.813
Subnet Mask
255.255.255.0
Default Gateway
135.792.46.001
The information in the
TCP/IP
section on your status sheet should match the network segment being used on the network that the computers belong to.
If the IP address in the
TCP/IP
section is 169.254.43.71 and the information is as shown below, the network is not releasing a TCP/IP address to the CX11NF.
IP Address
169.254.43.71
Subnet Mask
255.255.0.0
Default Gateway
(None)
Follow these steps to enable the CX11NF to accept a TCP/IP address:
Press the
Setup
button.
Use the
button to select
Host I/F Settings
, then press the
button.
Use the
button to select
Network Settings
, then press the
button.
Use the
button to select
Network I/F=On
, then press the
button.
Turn the CX11NF off, wait 1 minute, then turn it back on.
Reprint a network status sheet to verify that the CX11NF has obtained a TCP/IP address. The CX11NF should now be enabled for TCP/IP and available on the network segment.
Install the CX11NF software in network mode to print and scan from the network.

Printing a Status Sheet

faqs.question: When I press the B&W Start or Color Start button to make a copy, nothing happens. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
The CX11NF may not be in Copy mode when you are pressing the button (Print mode is the default mode). Make sure you press the
Copy
button before you press either
B&W Start
or
Color Start
.
Note:
If you don't press any button for more than 3 minutes, the CX11NF returns to Print mode.
Make sure paper is loaded in the MP tray or the optional Paper Cassette Unit. See
Loading Paper
.
Make sure your original is placed face-down on the document table or face-up in the Auto Document Feeder. See
Setting Your Originals
.
Note:
If you place documents in both in the Auto Document Feeder and on the document table, only the documents in the Auto Document Feeder will be scanned.

faqs.question: What sizes of documents can I copy or scan with my product?
faqs.answer:
When you use the document table, you can copy, fax, or scan any document up to size A4 (8.5” x 11.7”).
When you use the ADF (Auto Document Feeder):
You can copy or scan B5, A4, Letter, and Legal size documents
.
You can fax A4, Letter, and Legal size documents
.
Note:
If you fax an original smaller than Letter size, it is transmitted in Letter landscape.

faqs.question: It takes a long time to copy a document. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Select
B&W
as the copy type.
Select
With Border
as the layout type.*
Make sure
2-Sided Printing
is turned off.*
Select
Plain Paper
as the paper type.
Select
Draft
or
Standard
as the quality type.
Make sure
Dry Time
is set to
Standard
.*
* This step may not apply to your all-in-one.

faqs.question: When I try to copy using the High quality document type setting at the same time as the 2 Pages per Sheet setting, I get a memory error message. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
To use the
High quality
setting, your CX11NF should have at least 256MB of memory. If you're not sure how much memory your CX11NF has,
print a status sheet
and then
add memory
if necessary.

faqs.question: Why do I see the message Mem Overflow on my product's LCD screen?
faqs.answer:
The CX11NF doesn't have enough memory to print the job. Press the
B&W Start
or
Color Start
to resume printing, or press the
Cancel
button to cancel the print job.

faqs.question: Why do I see the message Check Transparency on my product's LCD screen?
faqs.answer:
There may be a mismatch between the loaded paper or transparencies and the printer driver setting for your paper or transparencies.
Also, paper may be jammed in the MP (multi-purpose) tray.
Clear jammed paper
if necessary.

faqs.question: Why do I get a Scanner Cover Open error when I turn on my product?
faqs.answer: The ADF cover should be closed when powering on the printer.

faqs.question: How do I edit speed dial recipients?
faqs.answer:
You can edit speed dial recipients by doing the following:
In the Speed Dial tab, select a registered recipient from the list.
Click the
Edit
button. You see the Edit Window:
Make the desired changes to the information. Then click
OK.
The changes are saved and displayed in the registered recipient list in the Speed Dial Tab.
To edit other registered recipients, repeat the above steps.

faqs.question: I'm having trouble sending or receiving faxes. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Make sure the printer's
LINE
port is connected to a telephone wall jack.
Verify that the telephone wall jack works by connecting a phone to it.
If the all-in-one is connected to a DSL phone line, a DSL filter must be connected to the phone jack. Contact your DSL provider for the necessary filter.
Make sure that your recipient's fax machine is turned on and working.
Make sure
paper is loaded correctly
.
If you're using
DRD
(Distinctive Ring Detection), try setting
DRD
to
OFF
or
ALL
. If the fax answers when turning off
DRD
, the ring pattern may be causing the problem. Contact your phone company.
If a telephone with an answering machine is connected to the all-in-one and you would like to set the all-in-one to automatically receive and print faxes,
set the number of rings
on the all-in-one to more than the answering machine, and turn
Auto Answer
mode on (on the all-in-one).
Turn call waiting off. Call waiting may disrupt an incoming or outgoing fax.
If the all-in-one does not receive a fax, verify that it's not connected to a PBX system. The ring signal on a PBX system can cause a problem. Contact your PBX administrator for support.
Note:
Because fax machines are designed to work over standard analog telephone lines, Epson does not guarantee that fax transmission will work over VOIP phone lines (cable systems such as Cox, Charter, Time Warner, Comcast, FIOS, Vonage).

faqs.question: How do I use an answering machine with my fax?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Make sure that your answering machine is connected to the EXT port on the Epson fax machine.
Set the number of rings on the answering machine.
Set the number of rings on the fax machine to a number greater than the answering machine (for example, if answering machine is set to 4, the fax must be set for 5 or more).
Ensure that the answering machine is set to answer and the fax machine is set to Auto Answer.
When the answering machine picks up a fax call, the fax machine listens on the line and if it detects the fax tones, it takes over the call and disconnects the answering machine.

faqs.question: How do I add my name to the sender information on my outgoing faxes?
faqs.answer:
To add your name to the sender information, you must use the Epson Speed Dial Utility. Follow the steps below:
Note:
The Epson Speed Dial Utility is compatible only with Windows computers. If you are using a Macintosh, you will not be able to add your name to your sender information.
Install the Speed Dial Utility (included on the CD-ROMs that came with your CX11NF).
Make sure the CX11NF is connected and is communicating with the driver.
Click
Start
and select
Programs
or
All Programs
.
Select
EPSON Speed Dial Utility
, then click
Speed Dial Utility
. A
Speed Dial Utility
window appears.
Select
Create New
(on the left side of the window).
Click the
Sender Information
tab (on the right side of the window).
Enter your name in the
Sender name
field.
Click
Send Record
.
When you see a window asking you
Send user data to the MFP?
, click
Yes
. Your sender information is uploaded to the CX11NF.
When you see a window containing the message
Upload completed
, click
OK
. Your name has now been added to the sender information in the CX11NF.
Click
Save
to save the sender name in the Speed Dial Utility, or click
Cancel
to exit the utility.
To include your sender information on your outgoing faxes,
activate the
Print Sender Info
setting
.
Editing Speed Dial Recipients
In the Speed Dial tab, select a registered recipient from the list.
Click the
Edit
button. You see the Edit window:
Make the desired changes to the information. Then click
OK.
The changes are saved and displayed in the registered recipient list in the Speed Dial Tab.
To edit other registered recipients, repeat the above steps.

Because fax machines are designed to work over standard analog telephone lines, Epson does not guarantee that fax transmission will work over VoIP phone lines (cable systems such as Cox, Charter, Time Warner, Comcast, FiOS, magicJack, and Vonage).
Internet traffic can interfere with faxing because VoIP communicates through the internet and not through standard analog telephone lines. The data sent over the internet for a fax is digitized into packets and this process can cause data loss.

faqs.question: Some or all of my printout is garbled. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
Make sure both ends of the interface cable are fully plugged in. The interface cable may not be securely connected.
Make sure you're using an interface cable with the correct specifications. If you're using a USB cable, make sure it is a shielded “AB” cable no more than 6.5 feet (2 meters) long.
Make sure you have the correct printer driver selected in your software.

faqs.question: My copy is blank, or images are missing or faded. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
If you're using the ADF (Auto Document Feeder) to load your original, make sure the ADF cover is closed firmly. If the ADF cover is open, the document table will be scanned instead of your originals and a blank copy may result.
For more help, see
Copies are blank, or images are missing or faded
and/or
Completely blank pages are output

faqs.question: The quality of my copies is not good. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Make sure you're using the correct type of paper for copying. The available paper types for copying are not the same as those for printing. Depending on the paper source, the following paper types are available for copying:
MP Tray: Plain paper, Letterhead, Recycled paper, Colored paper, Transparencies, Labels
Optional Paper Cassette Unit: Plain paper, Letterhead, Recycled paper, Colored paper
For more help with copy quality, see
Copy Quality Problems
.

faqs.question: Why are the colors of my scanned image wrong?
faqs.answer:
See
Colors differ from the original

faqs.question: My scans are being cropped (the edges are missing). What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure you place your original at least .06 inches (1.5 mm) away from the top and left edges of the document table (glass) to avoid image cropping.

faqs.question: My scanned image is blurry. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
See
The image is distorted or blurred

faqs.question: Why do dark lines appear in my prints when I use the ADF?
faqs.answer:
Dust may be collected on the glass and on some parts in the ADF. Follow these steps to remove the dust:
Open the document cover.
Use a lint free cloth to clean the document table glass.
Clean the white plastic paper guide and the document pad under the document cover.
Remove the edge of the white plastic paper guide from the slot on the right and clean underneath it.
Reinsert the plastic paper guide into the slot. Be sure to insert it into the correct position.
Close the document cover.

faqs.question: My product is new and all the colors are printing incorrectly. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Make sure the toner cartridges are installed in the correct slots. The back plate of each cartridge slot is color coded to match the toner color for that slot.
Yellow toner cartridge
Yellow toner slot

faqs.question: I want to enlarge an image that I'm scanning with Epson Scan. How do I obtain the best quality?
faqs.answer:
To obtain the best quality, you should resize your image when you're scanning instead of enlarging it later in an image-editing program.
For specific instructions on resizing your image when you're scanning, see
Selecting the Scan Size
.
Note:
If you plan to enlarge your image later in an image-editing program, you need to increase the
Resolution
setting to retain a high image quality after enlargement. Increase the resolution by the same amount you will increase the image size. For example, if the resolution is 300 dpi (dots per inch), but you will increase the image size by 200% in an image-editing program, change the
Resolution
setting to 600 dpi in Epson Scan.

faqs.question: The settings are grayed out in Epson Scan on my Mac. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Create a new user account using the instructions below.  If you are able to change the settings in Epson Scan using the new account but not with the old account, please contact Apple for possible solutions.
Click the Apple icon, then select
System Preferences
.
Under
System
, select
Accounts
.
If the padlock in the lower left corner is locked, click it to unlock it and enter the password when prompted.
Click the
+
to create a new account.
At the top, change the New Account field to
Administrator
.
Complete the required fields, then click
Create Account
.  (Do not set to automatically log in).
Close the Accounts screen, click on the Apple icon to log out, then log in as the new user.
Open Epson Scan.

faqs.question: The Print light does not turn on when I turn on the product. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure the power cord is plugged into both a power outlet and the CX11NF. Also, make sure the outlet is operational and not connected to a timer or switch.

faqs.question: The Print light is on but nothing prints. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
If your CX11NF won't print, you may have one of the following problems:
Your computer may not be securely connected to the CX11NF. Check the connection at both ends. If you're using a USB cable, connect the square end of the cable to the back of the CX11NF and the flat end of the USB cable to any open USB port on your computer.
Your application software may not be set up correctly. Make sure the CX11NF is selected in your software.
Your computer system's memory may be too small to handle the volume of data in your document. Try reducing the image resolution in your application software, or install more memory in your computer.

faqs.question: My product is connected to my computer with a USB cable, but the computer won't recognize it. Why?
faqs.answer:
Your CX11NF may not work properly if you use a USB cable other than the one supplied by Epson. Use the USB cable that comes with your product.
Also, the CX11NF may not work properly if you connect it to the computer through more than one hub. Connect the CX11NF directly to your computer's USB port, or through one hub only.

faqs.question: What is the difference between PBX and PSTN?
faqs.answer:
PBX (Private Branch Exchange) is used in office environments where 9 must be dialed to call an outside line (outside of the office building).
PSTN (Public Switched Telephone Network) is a standard phone line, similar to the one in your home.
The default Line Type setting is PSTN. Follow these steps to change it to PBX:

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
